assignments.brief_reason: Pair-consistency fairness rule about removing both when one is removed fits high-bar removal of toxic material.
Checking whether both sides make the same-level point emphasizes applying identical standards across viewpoints.
Explicit thresholds using tone/volatility and rage-bait as disqualifiers match toxicity/threat removal.
Trying to be equal by considering both sides aligns with applying the same moderation standard across viewpoints.
Reliance on gut instinct near the boundary is not a clear fit to any provided moderation-content themes.
Rule that banning one requires banning the other out of fairness matches consistent moderation across sides.
States content-based evaluation of the pair to apply the same standards regardless of perspective.
Gut feelings about negativity could relate to removing toxic content, but the mapping is indirect.
Using profanity and threats as cues aligns with allowing speech except when threats/violence or closely related bad language appear.
Perceived harmfulness is consistent with a higher-moderation bar that removes threatening/toxic content.
Free-speech fallback: keep despite disagreement unless posts seem harmful/inciting.
Opposes censorship but allows removal when posts are offensive toward a group (and mentions misinformation concerns)—violence/threat exception framing fits best among options.
General positivity about the task with no moderation rationale.
Using tone similarity across the pair to treat them the same reflects consistent standards across viewpoints.
Treating mirror posts as disrespectful/non-discursive is a procedural pair criterion, but it most resembles exclusion for harmful/toxic dynamics.
Allows name-calling under free-speech principle while drawing limits; best matches speech-with-exceptions category.
Side-by-side comparison to stay objective and treat both as the same kind of heated venting matches applying consistent criteria across sides.
Protects free speech by allowing heated arguments if there is merit/truth, with no blanket removal.
Decision is based on ideological identification/support rather than moderation logic.
Keep if productive/harmless; remove when too inflammatory or personal attacks—fits removing toxic/inflammatory content under a higher bar.
